subject: Math
subskill: Graph - Identify Inequality from Shaded Region
prompt: The triangle inequality theorem states that the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side. A triangle has two sides with lengths $9$ and $14$. Which inequality represents the possible lengths, $x$, of the third side of this triangle?
explanation: Choice C is correct. By the triangle inequality theorem, for a triangle with side lengths $9$, $14$, and $x$, all three of the following must hold: $9 + 14 > x$, $9 + x > 14$, and $14 + x > 9$. Simplifying $9 + 14 > x$ yields $x < 23$. Subtracting $9$ from both sides of $9 + x > 14$ yields $x > 5$. Subtracting $14$ from both sides of $14 + x > 9$ yields $x > -5$, which is automatically satisfied whenever $x > 5$. Combining the two binding constraints gives $5 < x < 23$.
